overview: Far East Horizon is a Hong Kong-headquartered, mainland China-focused financial leasing and industrial operations group that pairs a large RMB financial-leasing book with wholly owned industrial platforms in equipment operation (Horizon Construction Development) and private hospitals (Horizon Healthcare). It operates under a self-described 'finance + industry' model, serving corporate, SME, and urban-government customers across healthcare, engineering construction, machinery, chemicals, electronics, transportation/logistics and urban public utilities. The Company is listed on the HKEX Main Board (H-shares, HKD-quoted) but reports in RMB, with total assets of RMB371.0 billion and net interest-earning assets of RMB272.0 billion at FY2025 year-end.

business_model.summary: Revenue is split between (1) financial services — interest income from a financial-leasing/lending book plus advisory fee income — and (2) industrial operation — equipment-rental revenue from Horizon Construction Development (aerial work platforms, scaffolding/formwork, material assets) and hospital-operation revenue from Horizon Healthcare (25 controlled hospitals). The financial segment behaves like a non-bank lender: it earns a net interest spread (4.39% in FY2025) funded by bank borrowings and bond/ABS issuance, and increasingly by a faster-growing, higher-yield 'inclusive finance' (SME) book. The industrial segment is capital-intensive, generates rental/service revenue, and is more cyclical and property/construction-market sensitive.
business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B and B2G — large corporate/industry-leader customers and local-government/urban-investment platforms for traditional leasing; SMEs for the fast-growing inclusive-finance book; construction contractors and property developers for equipment rental; patients/insurers for hospital operations
business_model.geographic_mix: Overwhelmingly mainland China for financial services (Eastern China ~49% of interest income, Central ~16%, Southwest ~10%, Northern ~11%); Horizon Construction Development has 485 domestic outlets plus 77 overseas outlets across Malaysia, Vietnam, Indonesia, Thailand, Saudi Arabia, UAE and Turkey, with overseas revenue of RMB1.4bn (FY2025) growing faster than the domestic book

competitive_position.market_position: One of the largest non-bank-affiliated financial leasing companies in China by total assets and equity, ranked among the top 5 nationally including bank-backed peers (per CCXAP rating commentary); the broader industry (~RMB5.4 trillion contract balance) has been consolidating, with the number of leasing companies nationwide falling toward ~7,000 amid tighter regulation

moat_factors.description: Unlike most large Chinese leasing peers that are subsidiaries of state banks, Far East Horizon built scale independently, giving it more commercial flexibility but also a structurally higher funding cost than bank-backed competitors

Owning industrial operating assets (equipment rental fleet, hospitals) alongside the leasing book gives cross-selling, asset-recovery and risk-management advantages (e.g., repossessed equipment can be redeployed into the rental fleet) not available to pure financial lessors

moat_factors.factor: Long operating history and credit relationships
moat_factors.description: Over a decade of relationships with China Development Bank, Bank of China and other principal bankers, plus an A- international issuer rating (JCR), supports continued wholesale funding access

~200,000 aerial work platforms managed and ~560 outlets globally (485 domestic, 77 overseas) make it a top-10-15 global equipment-rental operator (11th on IRN100), with first-mover scale advantages in overseas emerging markets (Middle East, Southeast Asia)

A differentiated 'short-term, small-ticket, frequent, urgent' SME lending capability built over several years is scaling rapidly (interest income +125% in FY2025 to RMB3.5bn, +87% in H1 FY2026) and diversifying away from large-ticket traditional leasing

weaknesses: No deposit funding base (unlike bank-affiliated leasing peers), so funding cost is structurally higher and more sensitive to bond-market conditions

Industrial segment (equipment rental, hospitals) is directly exposed to China's construction/property downturn and healthcare reimbursement pressure, and has posted revenue declines for two consecutive periods
Smaller scale than the bank-sponsored leasing giants (ICBC Leasing, CDB Leasing, BoCom Leasing) which can cross-subsidize leasing economics with parent-bank balance sheets
Complex conglomerate structure (finance + equipment rental + hospitals) makes the stock harder for investors to value on a sum-of-the-parts basis and obscures segment-level capital allocation

growth_drivers: Inclusive finance (SME) business scaling rapidly with high growth in both asset balance and interest income, diversifying the loan book and lifting blended yield

Overseas expansion of Horizon Construction Development into Southeast Asia, Middle East (Saudi Arabia, UAE) and newer frontier markets (Kazakhstan, Morocco, Tanzania), which management flags as the key industrial growth driver while domestic equipment rental pricing stays under pressure

'Serving the city' urban-investment platform business (3+X framework: leasing, asset management, overseas business, plus other services) targeting restructuring of local government financing vehicles in economically vibrant regions

Five Key Areas of Finance strategic focus (technology, green, inclusive, pension, digital finance) aligned with policy priorities and PBOC-subsidized relending facilities, supporting continued access to cheaper targeted funding

Declining funding costs as PBOC maintains an accommodating policy stance (LPR cuts, reserve requirement cuts) and the Company optimizes its bond/ABS issuance mix, supporting net interest spread expansion
AI-enabled efficiency programs in Horizon Healthcare (diagnosis, treatment, hospital operations) and in leasing risk management/collections to lower cost-to-income ratio

business.description: Horizon Construction Development revenue fell 19.2% YoY in FY2025 and a further 6.0% in H1 FY2026 on weak domestic construction/property activity and equipment-rental price deflation; Horizon Healthcare revenue fell 12.7% in FY2025 on subdued medical investment and insurance reimbursement controls

Leasing book and advisory exposure concentrated in engineering construction, machinery, urban infrastructure and healthcare — sectors directly tied to China's property/construction downturn and local-government fiscal stress

Rapid build-out of equipment-rental outlets across emerging markets (Middle East, Southeast Asia, Africa, Central Asia) carries country, FX and operational risk, though overseas operations have so far been profitable and growing

The faster-growing SME lending book inherently carries higher credit risk than traditional large-ticket leasing; management has already tightened write-off policy (writing off at 30+ days overdue) and write-off losses on inclusive-business assets rose 153% YoY in FY2025

financial.description: Gearing ratio of ~83-84% and total liabilities of RMB311bn vs total equity of RMB60bn at FY2025 year-end is typical for a leasing business model but leaves limited equity cushion against asset-quality deterioration

No deposit base; funded via bank borrowings (RMB267bn) and capital-market issuance (corporate bonds, MTNs, super-short-term financial bonds, ABS), making cost and availability of funding sensitive to onshore/offshore credit market conditions

financial.risk: Rising effective tax rate from cross-border dividends
financial.description: Effective tax rate rose from 43.7% in FY2024 to 50.3% in FY2025 due to withholding tax on cross-border dividend distributions to overseas (Hong Kong) entities, structurally compressing net profit growth even when pre-tax profit is flat
RMB-denominated financials against an HKD-quoted stock; overseas borrowings and overseas industrial operations introduce some FX exposure, partially offset by overseas revenue growth

regulatory.description: The National Financial Regulatory Administration's new Measures for the Administration of Financial Leasing Business and Measures for Supervision and Rating of Financial Leasing Companies (2025/2026) require tighter focus on core leasing business, stricter risk controls, clearer leased-asset ownership, and stronger oversight of sale-leaseback funding — raising compliance costs and potentially constraining balance-sheet growth

Ongoing medical insurance cost control, volume-based procurement, and the Sanming medical reform are compressing hospital reimbursement economics nationally, pressuring Horizon Healthcare's revenue and margins

The number of licensed financial leasing companies in China continues to shrink (~7,020, down sharply YoY) and the national leasing contract balance has declined for multiple years, reflecting a structurally tightening regulatory and competitive environment, though this also favors well-capitalized survivors like Far East Horizon

macro.description: Real estate investment, construction GFA and new-construction GFA all fell double-digits YoY in H1 FY2026 (-18.0%, -12.5%, -23.4% respectively), directly depressing demand for Horizon Construction Development's equipment rental and pressuring asset quality in leasing exposure tied to construction/property-adjacent customers

macro.risk: Local government/urban investment platform fiscal stress
macro.description: Restructuring of China's urban investment and financing system creates both an opportunity (new integrated city-services business) and a risk (counterparty credit stress among local-government-linked customers)

Net interest spread and margin are sensitive to PBOC rate policy; a prolonged low-rate, accommodative environment has so far compressed funding costs faster than asset yields (benefiting NIM), but a tightening cycle or renewed stress in China's property-linked credit markets could reverse this
Slowing fixed-asset investment (-5.7% YoY in H1 FY2026) and weak private investment (-8.5%) signal a soft demand environment across most of the Group's core industrial end-markets

macro_factors.industry_outlook: China's financial leasing industry (~RMB5.38 trillion contract balance, declining ~1.5% YoY but with the pace of decline narrowing) is in a multi-year consolidation and regulatory tightening phase; equipment leasing/rental has domestic softness (especially property-linked construction) but strong overseas growth along Belt & Road markets; healthcare services sector is shifting from volume-driven to value-based, insurance-constrained care
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high — the financial-leasing book and industrial operations are both geared to China's construction, infrastructure and SME investment cycles; asset quality metrics (NPL ratio ~1.0%, overdue 30+ day ratio ~0.8%) have stayed stable through the downturn but bear watching
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate — net interest spread/margin benefit from PBOC rate cuts and declining bond yields (average funding cost fell to 3.79% in FY2025 from 4.06%), but a reversal in China's accommodative policy stance would compress margins
key_input_costs: Onshore/offshore bond and ABS issuance costs
Equipment capex (aerial work platforms, scaffolding, materials)

recent_developments.event: H1 FY2026 interim results: total revenue RMB18.04bn (+4.05% YoY), profit attributable to shareholders RMB2.22bn (+2.68% YoY); financial services revenue +9.69% YoY driven by inclusive finance (+86.75% YoY); industrial operation revenue -5.98% YoY; interim dividend of HK$0.25/share declared
Board changes: Mr. LIU Haifeng David retired as non-executive director (10 March 2026); company secretary transition from Ms. YUEN Wing Yan Winnie to Ms. YEUNG Siu Lam (11 March 2026)
FY2025 final dividend of HK$0.31/share recommended for distribution, bringing total FY2025 dividends to HK$0.56/share, a 61% payout ratio

FY2025 full-year results: revenue RMB35.79bn (-5.2% YoY) on industrial-segment weakness; profit attributable to shareholders RMB3.89bn (+0.67% YoY) as financial services growth offset industrial decline; NPL ratio improved to 1.03% from 1.07%; net interest margin rose to 4.83% from 4.48%; effective tax rate jumped to 50.3% from 43.7% on cross-border dividend withholding tax

Convertible bonds issued in July 2020 fully converted, adding ~430 million shares and RMB2.95bn to equity attributable to ordinary shareholders, diluting EPS but strengthening the capital base and lowering the gearing ratio

Continued overseas expansion of Horizon Construction Development — new outlets/trial operations launched in Kazakhstan, Morocco and Tanzania; global outlet count grew to 544-562 across mainland China, Hong Kong and 10 overseas countries

guidance.as_of: H1 FY2026 Interim Report (August 2026) / FY2025 Annual Report

items.target: ~60%+ of profit attributable to ordinary shareholders
items.notes: FY2025 payout ratio was 61%; management reiterated commitment to a 'steady' and 'generous' cash distribution policy going forward, though no specific numeric FY2026 target was issued

Management stated expectation that pre-provision operating profit will 'maintain steady growth' as the external market environment stabilizes, industrial operation scale gradually expands, and internal operating efficiency improves — a qualitative rather than numeric target
No explicit numeric guidance; H1 FY2026 NIM of 5.50% and spread of 5.04% were both up from H1 FY2025's 4.51%/4.06%, management citing structural mix shift toward higher-yield inclusive finance

items.target: Continued penetration of Middle East, Southeast Asia and new frontier markets (Kazakhstan, Morocco, Tanzania)
items.notes: No specific revenue or outlet-count target disclosed for FY2026, but management continues to flag overseas operations as 'a key growth driver' offsetting domestic softness

guidance.management_commentary: Management (Chairman and CEO Mr. KONG Fanxing) described 2025 as a year of 'steady and stable' financial structure despite industry fluctuations, with all business segments profitable. For 2026, management reiterated adherence to the 'finance + industry' strategy, continued commercial ecosystem iteration, and prioritization of safe and stable operations, asset quality and liquidity management over aggressive balance-sheet growth. No formal numeric revenue or EPS guidance for FY2026 was found in the filings reviewed; guidance is primarily qualitative/directional.

bull_case: Inclusive finance (SME) business is scaling rapidly (interest income +125% in FY2025, +87% in H1 FY2026) at structurally higher yields, diversifying the book and driving net interest margin expansion even as the legacy traditional leasing book stays flat

Asset quality has remained stable-to-improving through a tough industrial downturn (NPL ratio down to ~1.0%, overdue 30+ day ratio ~0.8%, provision coverage >225%), suggesting underwriting discipline rather than credit deterioration masked by growth

High and consistent dividend payout (~60% of profit, HK$0.56/share FY2025) combined with a low reported P/E (~7x per third-party aggregators) offers a value/income case if the industrial segment stabilizes

Overseas equipment-rental expansion (Middle East, Southeast Asia, new frontier markets) is already profitable and growing, providing a structural offset to China's domestic construction weakness and a longer-run diversification story

Declining funding costs in an accommodative PBOC rate environment are expanding net interest spread (4.39% FY2025 vs 4.00% FY2024; 5.04% H1 FY2026), a direct tailwind to profitability that is independent of asset growth
bear_case: Industrial segment (equipment rental + hospitals) has posted consecutive periods of double-digit revenue declines, directly tied to China's structurally weak property/construction sector with no clear domestic turning point yet

Effective tax rate jumped to 50.3% in FY2025 from 43.7%, driven by cross-border dividend withholding tax, compressing net profit growth even when operating performance is stable — a drag that could persist or worsen
High leverage (gearing ~84%) with no deposit funding base means the Company is more exposed than bank-affiliated leasing peers to swings in wholesale credit market conditions and borrowing costs

Rapid growth of the inclusive finance (SME) book, while currently well-provisioned, is an unseasoned higher-risk credit exposure whose true loss rates will only be tested through a full macro cycle, and write-off losses on this book already rose 153% YoY in FY2025

Tightening financial-leasing sector regulation (new national measures on core-business focus, risk controls, leaseback funding oversight) could constrain balance-sheet flexibility and raise compliance costs across the industry

Complex multi-segment conglomerate structure (leasing + equipment rental + hospitals) makes the business harder to value cleanly and could obscure capital-allocation decisions or cross-segment risk transfer
